query_text: How do you create eye contact with someone with a lazy eye?

message.content:
Based on my research, here are practical strategies for creating comfortable eye contact with someone who has a lazy eye (amblyopia or strabismus):

## Focus on the Person, Not the Eye Condition

The most important principle is to **treat the person normally** and not make their eye condition the center of attention. People with lazy eye are often self-conscious about it, so drawing attention to it can increase discomfort.

## Use General Eye Contact Best Practices

Several techniques work well for all conversations, including those with someone who has a lazy eye:

- **Look at the bridge of the nose or forehead** if direct eye contact feels awkward for either of you. This creates the appearance of eye contact without the stress of focusing on one specific eye [1][5]

- **Use the triangle technique**: Imagine an inverted triangle connecting both eyes and the mouth. Rotate your gaze between these three points every few seconds [5]

- **Follow the 50/70 rule**: Maintain eye contact about 50% of the time when speaking and 70% when listening [5]

- **Hold gaze for 4-5 seconds at a time**, then glance away briefly before returning [5]

## Be Adaptable and Respectful

- **Let them lead**: If they naturally favor one eye for focusing, follow their lead rather than trying to force contact with a specific eye [2]

- **Don't point it out or ask about it** unless they bring it up themselves [6]

- **Maintain normal conversational flow**: Excessive concern about "getting it right" can make interactions more awkward [6]

## Consider Their Perspective

Many adults with lazy eye experience self-consciousness and may have developed their own strategies for managing social interactions [6]. Some may avoid eye contact altogether due to past negative experiences. Being patient and creating a comfortable atmosphere matters more than perfect eye contact mechanics.

## When in Doubt

If you're unsure, **looking slightly above or between the eyes** at the forehead or bridge of the nose is generally the safest approach that appears natural to the other person while avoiding any awkwardness about which eye to focus on [1][5].

6. https://myoptometristcalgary.ca/blog/A+Comprehensive+Guide+Coping+with+Lazy+Eye+as+an+Adult+Strategies+and+Support/182
